memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: This is the regular burnt offering instituted at Mount Sinai as a pleasing aroma, a food offering presented to the LORD. The accompanying drink offering is to be a quarter of a hin of fermented drink with each lamb. Pour out the drink offering to the LORD at the sanctuary. - Num 28:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Along with the daily lamb came a drink offering, poured out at the sanctuary before the Lord. This offering, established back at Sinai, was a fragrant gift presented to God. The pouring out of the drink offering was a vivid picture of devotion completely surrendered, poured out and held back for nothing.

There is rich meaning in this image of pouring out. To pour out a drink offering was to give something entirely, letting it soak into the ground with nothing kept in reserve. It spoke of a wholehearted devotion that offers everything to God. Worship, at its truest, is not partial but poured out.

We remember again that these ceremonial forms belonged to Israel under the old covenant and find their fulfilment in Christ. We do not pour out literal drink offerings today. But the picture of a life poured out for God remains deeply instructive. God is worthy of our complete surrender, not merely our leftovers.

Most wonderfully, this points to Christ, who poured out His life unto death for us (Isa 53:12). And in response, the apostle Paul spoke of his own life being poured out like a drink offering in service to God (Phil 2:17). In Christ, we are called to offer our whole selves as living sacrifices, poured out in glad devotion. What are you holding back that God is calling you to pour out for Him?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you offer God your whole self, or only your leftovers?
2. How does Christ's poured-out life inspire your devotion?
3. What might it mean to pour out your life for God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You poured out Your life completely for me. Teach me to hold nothing back but to offer my whole self as a living sacrifice, poured out in glad and grateful devotion to You. Amen.
